p.x:
Setting aside the framing of "fixing" or "curing" as no method/technique is a silver bullet – yes, it's possible to unlock huge boosts in well-being in the form of increased joy/peace/focus/emotional fluidity/etc. 

The way to stop running on "Feels Bad" is to investigate negative emotions with enough love and curiosity to fully feel them and discover the positive intentions they hold for you. Sources of tension are often useful reminders. Maybe they're protecting you from something hurtful, or gesturing to your values, or trying to ensure your survival. They honestly don't get enough credit for what they do, especially when approached adversarially and treated like they're the "problem," which often just tightens the knot further.

Once you discover they were on your side all along and stop shooting yourself in the foot, there's nothing to "do," no extra step, to "Feel Good." Living from an openhearted and accepting place feels effortless, because by welcoming the most difficult parts of yourself you have signaled to yourself that difficult experiences are not to be feared. Everything is welcome.

read through dfw's 2005 "this is water" speech b/c i was linked to it recently. interesting both as advice and as a cultural artifact. stray thoughts (i don't know much about dfw, although gpt-5.5 told me a few things):

 - this is considerably more interesting than the fish story in isolation, dfw tells that story as part of a larger arc about what specifically he thinks the water is and why it's important to notice it

 - dfw asserts very strongly that the "natural, hard-wired default setting" of the human mind is total self-centeredness and that it takes constant repeated effort to overcome this and consider the possibility that other people exist and have interiorities and deserve compassion. basically the entire speech is an exhortation to do this. i simply do not agree! even very young children display natural empathy and concern for others if it isn't stamped out. we innately possess the ability to sense and care about other people. it does suggest that this is how dfw experienced his own life. gpt-5.5 thinks this likely comes from his experiences in AA. this stuff is probably helpful for a lot of people but setting up the rest of your adult life as an eternal struggle between a goodself and a badself does not, i think, ultimately work (and sadly it does not appear to have worked for dfw)

 - he takes for granted that his audience (the 2005 graduating class of kenyon college) will have "comfortable, prosperous, respectable" adult lives and have "challenging, white-collar, college-graduate" jobs, and that their problem is going to be how to overcome the nihilism this might produce, american beauty style. which. lol. lmao. probably the bit that's aged the worst? 20 years later it appears to be uncertain whether the graduating class of any given college will be able to read

 - his description of "an average adult day" does not contain a mention of even television, let alone a computer or the internet. it would be fascinating to see what he would've made of social media. it's like everything he was afraid of about TV but so, so much worse

 - the bit about worship is great, maybe the part that's aged the best? no notes

 - several of his talking points remind me of @visakanv which makes me really wish he'd lived long enough to encounter twitter

 - it feels like he is constantly grappling with proto-buddhist ideas (when i suggested this gpt-5.5 described him as "especially obsessed with dukkha") but without any of the language or relevant experience. you have to wonder if one of those zen-for-addiction programs could've really helped him

 - the bit about "the so-called real world of men and money and power" also feels dated to me, maybe to the '80s or '90s? this kind of "commercialism is the great satan" stuff. it all feels very quaint now. whatever we've got going on these days "commercialism" no longer feels like a useful way of looking at it

 - overall the overwhelming impression i get is of a genuine spiritual seeker. this guy really wanted to know what was up. he wanted to know what was really going on and how to be a good person and do and see real things and not fake things. i have to respect that. makes me more interested in reading infinite jest sometime

someone built an OPENSOURCE MILITARY RADAR that tracks multiple targets up to 20km away

its called AERIS-10, full github repo schematics, PCB layouts, FPGA code, python GUI, everything under MIT license

commercial phased array radar starts at $250,000. military surplus is $10,000-50,000 but its decades old analog junk with no electronic beam steering

this does electronic beam steering at 10.5GHz, pulse compression, doppler processing, multi-target tracking on a real time map

two versions: 3km range with patch antenna array, 20km range with 32x16 slotted waveguide array and GaN AMPLIFIERS

custom frequency synthesizer, 16 front-end chips, FPGA doing all signal processing, GPS and IMU for ACCURATE target coordinates when the platform moves

all gerber files included so you can order the PCBs and build it yourself

one person built what defense contractors charge a quarter MILLION for and open sourced it
